svg.title: Registration-first bootstrap and bounded authority distribution
svg.desc: Trusted setup establishes tenant context. Auth and application permission and scope contracts are registered before initial grants are validated. Maximum intended tenant authority is explicitly assigned to the initial human administrator, who then administers users, groups, dependent grants, and membership under ordinary authorization rules.
svg.text: Bootstrap: register first, then establish authority
Q-039–Q-042 registration · Q-113 trusted setup · Q-114 maximum starting authority
1. Trusted setup + tenant context
Establish the setup trust; no grant may authorize its own creation.
Exact trust procedure and root-establishment evidence remain to be specified.
2. Register supported permission and scope contracts
Include Auth's administrative contracts and the relevant application contracts.
Declare the compatibility-validation mode; enabled means every grant is checked.
Registration defines valid contracts. It does not itself give anyone access.
3. Validate and establish maximum intended initial authority
Registered permissions + maximum scope {} inside the trusted tenant.
No wildcard syntax, cross-tenant access, or bootstrap exemption from contract validation.
4. Explicitly make the initial human administrator a recipient
Valid assignment(s), with explicit membership if a group-held route is used.
A stored grant definition alone supplies no access; the initial recipient format remains open.
5. Ordinary authorized administration
Create users/groups · assign equal or narrower grants · manage membership.
Members receive valid group authority, preserving its supporting lineage.
Always: tenant isolation · administrative + source checks · parent/team ceilings
Scope AND · status/validity · explicit adoption · human-dependent automation
Logical dependency flow, not a prescribed API sequence or a completed bootstrap implementation.
